finding.claim: The /mirror endpoint fetches a caller-supplied URL. The only check is a suffix match, `host.endswith("example.com")`, which is not strict set membership. The check has no leading dot, and the defined ALLOWED_SUFFIX (".example.com") is never used. An attacker can register or use `evilexample.com`, `attackerexample.com` or `example.com.evil.net`-style hosts that end in the string, and make the server request an attacker-chosen host. The check is also weak against internal names ending in example.com. Scheme is unrestricted, so only http and https are reachable through httpx. The response length is returned to the caller, which gives a partial oracle. Redirects are not followed because httpx defaults to follow_redirects=False. Impact: the server can be made to request attacker-controlled hosts and DNS names that resolve to internal addresses (DNS rebinding or attacker-owned records pointing at 169.254.169.254 or RFC-1918), with the response length reflected back. Severity is MEDIUM, since the check blocks literal IPs and arbitrary unrelated hosts.

finding.guards_checked: The endswith("example.com") hostname check is bypassable with evilexample.com. ALLOWED_SUFFIX is defined but unused. There is no scheme restriction, no IP or CIDR blocking and no authentication. Redirect following is off by default in httpx, so that avenue is closed. /ping at line 23 uses a hardcoded URL and is not a finding.

verdict.guard_found: host.endswith("example.com") at mirror.py:13, a suffix check with no leading dot. It does not close the finding. ALLOWED_SUFFIX at line 7 is unused. There is no scheme check, no IP blocking and no auth.
verdict.reason: The `url` query parameter (mirror.py:11) reaches `c.get(url)` at mirror.py:16 and only passes the suffix check `host.endswith("example.com")` at mirror.py:13, so `evilexample.com` is accepted and the response length is returned at line 17. The trace has one inaccuracy: the claim says "/ping at line 23 uses a hardcoded URL", but the `/ping` handler is at line 20 and the hardcoded URL is on line 23, so the line reference is correct. All other trace lines match the code. The claim that `example.com.evil.net` bypasses the check is wrong, since that host does not end in "example.com", but `evilexample.com` is enough to confirm the finding.
